title: Research notes: George Garvin Brown and Old Forester
summary: Sources for Brown’s life, the 1870 launch of Old Forester in sealed bottles, the disputed name, Brown-Forman, and the Prohibition-era medicinal permit.

items.text: Born Munfordville Sept. 2, 1846; Louisville 1862; Male High School; wholesale drug salesman; first president National Liquor Dealers’ Association 1894; anti-Prohibition book 1910; died 1917, buried Cave Hill.
1870: J. T. S. Brown and Brothers with half-brother J. T. S. Brown Jr.; Brown-Forman name adopted 1890 for partner and bookkeeper George Forman.
Sealed glass bottles against adulteration; signed labels; trademarked; first sold in pharmacies.
Name: usual account Dr. William Forrester; ExploreKYHistory notes others claim Nathan Bedford Forrest. Flagged as contested.
One of six Kentucky brands bottled for medicinal use during Prohibition.
Cut from brief: ‘at first about 90 proof’ (not in sources). ‘First bottled bourbon’ kept only as ExploreKYHistory’s claim.
Old Forester Distillery at 119 W. Main St., its 1880s home, on Louisville’s Whiskey Row.

timeline.event: Old Forester launched in sealed bottles.
